vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.tool: Applies a group of Minecraft and VulkanMod settings for the selected performance target.
vulkanmod.options.advCulling.tooltip: Use a culling algorithm that might improve performance by reducing the number of non visible chunk sections rendered.
vulkanmod.options.ao.subBlock.tooltip: ON (Sub-block): Enables smooth lighting for non full block (experimental).
vulkanmod.options.entityCulling.tooltip: Enables culling for entities on not visible sections.
vulkanmod.options.frameQueue.tooltip: Higher values might help stabilize frametime but will increase input lag.
vulkanmod.options.indirectDraw.tooltip: Reduces CPU overhead but increases GPU overhead. Enabling it might help in CPU limited systems. Unavailable on Intel GPUs and devices without multi-draw-indirect support.
vulkanmod.options.lodGpuCulling.tooltip: Culls distant LOD terrain cells on the GPU using frustum and depth-based occlusion tests before vertex shading. Only applies when a LOD companion mod is active and Indirect Draw is enabled.
vulkanmod.options.occlusionCulling.toolt: Skips rendering terrain, entities and LOD that are fully hidden behind other geometry, using a small depth grid of the previous frame. Replaces the old culling toggles.
vulkanmod.options.adaptiveChunkUploads.t: Adjusts chunk upload work from recent frame time to reduce stutter while moving or flying.
vulkanmod.options.chunkFadeIn.tooltip: Newly loaded chunks dither in smoothly over the distant terrain instead of appearing instantly.
vulkanmod.options.uniqueOpaqueLayer.tool: Use a unique render layer for opaque terrain to improve performance.
vulkanmod.options.particleCulling.toolti: Cull redundant particles based on distance, player FOV, and maximum same-type count budgets.
vulkanmod.options.blockEntityCulling.too: Cull block entities (chests, signs, spawners, etc.) that are outside the camera frustum or further than 96 blocks.
vulkanmod.options.leavesCulling.tooltip: Cull adjacent interior faces of leaf blocks to significantly improve performance in forests.
vulkanmod.options.renderScale.tooltip: The resolution the world is rendered at, as a percentage of the window. Lower means more frames and a softer image.
vulkanmod.options.vsrPreset.tooltip:
Renders the world below the window resolution, then reconstructs it to full size. Quality renders at 77%, Balanced at 67%, Performance at 50%, each with the sharpening that suits it. Custom lets you set the internal resolution and the sharpening yourself.

This only helps when the GPU is the bottleneck, which in practice means with shaders enabled. On vanilla rendering the GPU is barely loaded and lowering the internal resolution costs image quality for no frame rate at all.
vulkanmod.options.vsrBackend.tooltip:
How the internal resolution is reconstructed.

Bilinear is the plain reference filter: cheapest and softest.
FSR 1 reconstructs edges before sharpening: the crispest single frame, but high contrast edges can shimmer while the camera moves.
VTU accumulates several frames to rebuild detail: the most stable in motion, and it needs shaders to be enabled. Without them it falls back to FSR 1.
vulkanmod.options.vsrSharpness.tooltip: Contrast adaptive sharpening applied after reconstruction. It only affects edges, never flat areas, and never overshoots into halos. Set it to 0% to disable it.
vulkanmod.options.shadersEnabled.tooltip: Enable Volcanic's native Vulkan post-processing effects.
vulkanmod.options.horizonFog.tooltip: Smoothly fades distant terrain into the sky right at the render distance edge to hide chunk borders. Lower values pull the fog closer to the edge and make it thinner; Off disables it entirely.
vulkanmod.options.optimizedShadows.toolt: Render shadows at half resolution for a large performance gain. Slightly softer shadow edges.
vulkanmod.options.disableHiDPI.tooltip: macOS: render at the display's logical resolution instead of the full Retina resolution. Much faster, slightly softer image. Requires restart.
